lead: An agent manager doesn't have to become a lawyer, but needs to know what already applies, what has a deadline, what is under discussion and who owns each item. This lesson is short on purpose: it builds your area's compliance timeline and shows that the program's pieces already cover much of the evidence a regulation or a client will ask for.
objetivo: build the compliance timeline for your area: what already applies, what has a date, what is under discussion, and who looks after each item.

aprende.t: What already applies and what has a set date
How to handle what was only reported
What reaches you through the customer before it reaches you through the law
Which pieces of the program already serve as evidence

hero_alt: Desk by the window with a closed laptop, a paper calendar with colored squares, a folder with dividers and reading glasses; in the background, a person reads a document.

secoes.sub: Each item goes into a column, with a source, a date and an owner. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: What applies now. In Brazil, the LGPD applies to all personal data the agent touches: customer conversations, records, phone numbers. In the European Union, the AI literacy obligation (the team understanding enough about the AI it uses) already applies. The details, with articles and dates, are in the Profissional 2030 Base course.

What has a set date. Under the EU AI Act, the high-risk rules in Annex III were postponed to 02/12/2027 by the Digital Omnibus package of 07/24/2026. It applies to anyone who sells or uses AI in the European market.

What was reported and is not a rule. In Brazil, PL 2338/2023 was reported as stalled in the Chamber of Deputies. This is a secondary source: the bill's official record was not consulted. It goes on the timeline as "watch," never as an obligation.

What a large customer asks for before any law does: a supplier questionnaire about AI use, data and controls. The ISO/IEC 42001 standard (AI management system) shows up in these questionnaires. Having the pieces from this program ready shortens your answer.

secoes.legenda: Regulation facts from the October 2026 market overview (INEMA). This is not legal advice: if you are unsure about your obligation, the company's legal team decides.

secoes.sub: The details of the rules are in Profissional 2030 Base; here is what the manager does with them.

texto: Each item on the timeline has its source and the date of the source. Anything that only showed up in a blog or in an article citing another article goes in as "reported, check it", with the date of the news.
A timeline ages fast: the Digital Omnibus changed EU AI Act dates in 2026. Set the next review, every three months.

exemplo.texto: "PL 2338/2023: reported as stalled in the Chamber (article of 08/24/2026, secondary source). Owner: Carlos with the accounting firm. Review in January 2027."

texto: The 02/12/2027 date applies to anyone who sells or uses AI in the European market. Horizonte sells in the interior of São Paulo: today, it doesn't apply. Write that on the timeline, with the reason, instead of deleting the item.
If the company ever sells abroad, the item changes columns. That's why it stays on record.

exemplo.texto: At Horizonte it is not a legal obligation, but it is a cheap good practice: the team's training (the G1 training track) is the literacy.

passos.sub: the manager does not interpret the law
texto: Call whoever handles legal matters when: the agent decides something about people (credit, hiring), data leaves the country, a customer asks for a written statement, or you're unsure whether a rule applies to you.
Your role is to have the timeline, the owners and the evidence organized. The legal opinion belongs to someone else.

exemplo.texto: The support summary sends customer conversations to a foreign service without a contract (F10). That goes to legal and to the LGPD lesson in Professional 2030 Base.

passos.titulo: The advantage of having done the program
texto: When a customer or a rule asks "show me how you control AI," the answer is pieces you already have: the responsibility matrix, the identity and log checklist, the evaluation set, the dashboard and the version history.
Put them in one folder with an index. The next compliance question becomes a lookup in the folder, not a project.

exemplo.texto: Matrix (lesson 1) · checklist and access review (lesson 2) · 30 cases and result by version (lesson 3) · dashboard (lesson 4) · cycles and history (lessons 5 and 6).

secoes.sub: A one-page timeline and the evidence folder index. The next tab shows Horizonte's.

exercicios.texto: Without looking at the tab, build the timeline for Horizonte's sales area using the template. Use the four columns, the lab failures that touch personal data, and what a large customer might ask for. Run the review prompt.
exercicios.pronto: the timeline has at least 6 items across the 4 columns; each has a source with a date, "does it apply to us" with a reason, an owner and a next step; PL 2338 is marked "reported, check it"; and the next review date is written down.

exercicios.texto: Build your area's timeline and the evidence folder index with the pieces you already have from this program. Take the questions the prompt flagged to whoever handles legal matters.
exercicios.pronto: the timeline is saved with owners and a next review; the folder index points to at least 5 pieces that already exist; and the questions to legal were sent, with a date.

secoes.sub: 3 questions. The explanation appears after you try.

perguntas.p: How does PL 2338/2023 go into the timeline?
opcoes: Under discussion: reported as stalled, secondary source
As an obligation with a date, so the company can get ahead
It does not go in, because Congress has not approved it yet
perguntas.explica: What was reported goes in to be monitored, with the source and the date of the news, but never as a rule that obliges.

perguntas.p: Horizonte only sells in inland São Paulo state. What should you do with the EU AI Act item?
opcoes: Delete it from the timeline, because it doesn't apply to the company
Treat it as an obligation, to be safe, until legal weighs in
Keep it, marked "does not apply today," with the reason written down
perguntas.explica: Recording why something doesn't apply is as useful as recording what does: if the company ever sells abroad, the item changes columns.

perguntas.p: A hotel chain sends a questionnaire about how Horizonte controls AI. Where do you start?
opcoes: Buy a market certification before answering
From the evidence folder with the program's pieces
Answer that the company doesn't use AI in its orders yet
Ask the model vendor to answer on behalf of the company
perguntas.explica: The matrix, checklist, evaluation, dashboard and history already answer much of it. Whatever is missing becomes an item with an owner; whatever is legal goes to legal.

itens.texto: What already applies, with a date, what is under discussion, and what the customer requires.
A fact with a source; what was only reported goes in as "check it".
Each item has an owner; the whole row is reviewed every 3 months.
The pieces from the program answer most of the questions.
